cues.en: But as the abstractions become more robust, failures become rare, that's great, but the failures become worse.

cues.en: And again, this is that curse of the of that intermediate skier.

cues.en: As the as the abstractions become more robust, we are tempted to believe that the systems are infallible.

cues.en: And yet they are not infallible, in fact they are most dangerous in that we are thinking of them um as as infallible.

cues.en: Um and these failures, when this whole system fails, you are likely going to have failures in disjoint sub components, disjoint services, disjoint microservices.

cues.en: Of note, the light that sits on the control panel, indicating that the the that that the pilot operated relief valve is open, goes dark.

cues.zh: 这是一场 UI 灾难。
cues.en: That this was a UI disaster.

cues.zh: 那盏灯熄灭，并不是在泄压阀关闭的时候，而操作员们原以为是这样。
cues.en: That light goes dark, not when the relief valve closes, which is what the operators believed.

cues.zh: 那盏灯熄灭，是在电磁线圈通电、以关闭泄压阀的时候。
cues.en: That light goes dark when power has been applied to the solenoid to close the relief valve.

cues.zh: 我下达了关闭泄压阀的指令。
cues.en: I told the relief valve to close.

cues.zh: 而不是“泄压阀已关闭”。
cues.en: Not the relief valve is closed.

cues.zh: 操作员们被误导了。
cues.en: The operators were being lied to.

cues.zh: 他们其实还有其他办法弄清楚发生了什么，但他们没有。
cues.en: And they had other ways of figuring out what was going on, but they didn't.

cues.zh: 出于一些其实非常可以理解的原因，而且在最终调查结论中，操作员们实际上被认定没有责任，因为这个状况实在太难判断了。
cues.en: For reasons that are actually very understandable and in the final findings of this, the operators were actually uh held blameless because this was such a a difficult condition to figure out.

cues.zh: 反应堆那边，如果你知道那个泄压阀其实卡在开启位置。
cues.en: That the reactor, if you knew that the the the relief valve was actually stuck open.

cues.zh: 嗯，然后一切就都说得通了。
cues.en: Um then everything made sense.

cues.zh: 而且你实际上一直在把这些蒸汽、这些冷却剂漏出去，嗯，而且值得注意的是，你看下面有那个排水箱和那个爆破片，对吧？
cues.en: And you were actually losing all of this steam, all of this coolant um out and and notably, you see there was that drain tank down there and that rupture disk?

cues.zh: 所有这些冷却剂都流进那个排水箱，排水箱溢出，爆破片破裂，安全壳底部到处都是水，关于这个的警报响个不停，但所有这些警报都被忽略了，因为还有太多其他警报在响。
cues.en: All this coolant goes into that drain tank, that drain tank overflows, the rupture disk breaks, and there's water all over the bottom of the containment unit, alerts alerts going off about that, all those alerts are being ignored because there's so many other alerts going off.

cues.zh: 而这就是那种思路：哦，我们监控一切，我们对一切报警，这个，你懂的，监控一切，对一切报警。
cues.en: And this is the the whole idea of like, oh, we monitor everything, like we alert everything, this, you know, monitor everything, alert on everything.

cues.zh: 好吧，当然，但别以为你的警报和监控能替代对系统运作方式的理解。
cues.en: Okay, sure, but don't think that your alerts and your monitoring are a substitute for understanding the way the system works.

cues.zh: 有时我们会有这种告警、报警和监控的“教会”。
cues.en: Sometimes we have this church of alert and alerting and monitoring.

cues.zh: 我们相信，只要监控它，只要对它告警，就已经避免了灾难。
cues.en: And we believe that simply by monitoring it, simply by alerting upon it, we have averted disaster.

cues.zh: 这正是核工业在70年代末的想法。
cues.en: That's exactly what the nuclear industry thought in the late 70s.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，是那个已经消亡的核工业。
cues.en: The late nuclear the the nuclear industry by the way, the late nuclear industry.

cues.zh: 于是核工业被三里岛事件摧毁，再也没恢复过来。
cues.en: So the nuclear industry was destroyed by 3 Mile Island and never recovered.

cues.zh: 尽管那起事故其实并没有那么严重。
cues.en: Even though the incident was actually not that serious.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，其他领域发生过很多严重得多的事故；这起事故没那么严重，但它确实因为种种原因摧毁了核电。
cues.en: From a I mean, there are many many we've had many incidents in other domains that are much more serious, this incident was not that serious, but it did destroy nuclear power for a lot of reasons.

cues.zh: 呃，我特别喜欢那份特别报告里的这个发现，因为天哪，这感觉太适用于我们当下了。
cues.en: Uh, and I love this finding from the the the the the special report because boy, does this feel current for us.

cues.zh: 看着面板上一盏闪烁的指示灯，或听到一声警报响——更别说一堆警报——就立刻理清到底发生了什么，这很难。
cues.en: It's a difficult thing to look at a winking light on a board or hear a pinging alarm, not several of them, and immediately draw any sort of rational picture of something happening.

cues.zh: 警报和提醒越多，你就越是让操作员感官超载。
cues.en: And the more alarms and alerts you have, the more you are creating sensory overload for the operator.

cues.zh: 而且操作员看到的就越可能是一个告警——或者说监控警报——它更多是症状，而不是原因。
cues.en: And the more likely it is that the operator will be looking at an alert an alert or or or a monitoring alarm that is symptom more than cause.

cues.zh: 这并不是说你不该监控，显然你应该监控。
cues.en: This is not to say that you shouldn't monitor, obviously you should.

cues.zh: 我们应该监控系统，也应该针对系统设置告警。
cues.en: We should monitor our systems, we should alert on them.

cues.zh: 只是别骗自己，别以为这样一来我们就避免了一次宕机。
cues.en: Just don't fool yourself, don't delude yourself into thinking that we that we have avoided an outage as a result.

cues.zh: 所以我们也有许多相同的问题。
cues.en: So we suffer from many of the same problems.

cues.zh: 我们正承受着 70 年代核电那种傲慢带来的后果。
cues.en: We suffer from from the arrogance of nuclear power in the 70s.

cues.zh: 呃，我们兴高采烈地部署这些分布式系统，抱着一种错误想法：它们不知怎么就永远不会故障。
cues.en: Um, we are gleefully deploying these distributed systems with this this erroneous idea that they somehow can't fail.

cues.zh: 认为它们运行在多台计算机上，所以万无一失。
cues.en: That they're infallible because they're running on more than one computer.

cues.zh: 可事实证明，有些东西能同时影响多台计算机。
cues.en: It's like it turns out there are things that can affect more than one computer.

cues.zh: 相信我，我深有体会。
cues.en: Trust me, I know.

cues.zh: 呃，说的就是我。
cues.en: Um, it is me, as they say.

cues.en: Um.

cues.zh: 那这意味着什么？
cues.en: So what does it mean?

cues.zh: 那么，当这些东西出故障时，我们到底该怎么调试？
cues.en: So how how do we actually debug these things when they fail?

cues.zh: 嗯，我们必须想明白的一点是：我们得在生产环境里调试它们。
cues.en: Well, one of the things we have to wrap our brains around is that we will need to debug them in production.

cues.zh: 作为软件开发者，你必须这么做。
cues.en: You will need as a software developer.

cues.zh: 我知道，作为软件开发者，你只会想：这问题能不能赶紧消失？
cues.en: And I know as if you're a software developer, you're just like, can this problem please just go away?

cues.zh: 我能先回去吗，请让我回到刚才那张小图，我知道，不对。
cues.en: Can I just go, please, can I just go back to my little I know, no.

cues.zh: 这个问题躲不掉。我们需要真正去调试生产环境中的软件。
cues.en: This problem can't go away. We need to actually debug the software in production.

cues.zh: 而这其实引出了一个更深层的问题：我们到底该怎么调试？
cues.en: And that that prompts actually a deeper question, how do we actually debug?

cues.zh: 抽象地说，调试就是我们理解系统的过程。
cues.en: So in the abstract, debugging is the process by which we understand the system.

cues.zh: 我认为这是——这是我们在看待调试的方式上的一个重要区别，我们看待它的方式，与传统上被看待的方式之间的区别。
cues.en: And I think that this is uh this is a very kind of important difference in the way we view debugging, the way versus the way it's been viewed traditionally.

cues.zh: 调试不仅仅是把 bug 消除掉的行为。
cues.en: Debugging is not merely the act of making bugs go away.

cues.zh: 它是理解的行为，是获取关于系统如何运作的知识，新的知识。
cues.en: It is the act of understanding, gaining knowledge, new knowledge about the way the system works.

cues.zh: 这才是调试。
cues.en: That's what debugging is.

cues.zh: 而我们所理解的行为，是我们想要避免的特定的病态行为。
cues.en: And the behavior that we're understanding is particular pathological behavior that that we want to avoid.

cues.zh: 现在，理解系统里的行为这整件事，是啊，我们以前就干过。
cues.en: Now, this whole idea of like understanding behavior in a system, yeah, we've done that before.

cues.zh: 这就叫科学。
cues.en: That's called science.

cues.zh: 科学。
cues.en: Science.

cues.zh: 我们有自然世界。
cues.en: We have the natural world.

cues.zh: 我们想理解它，想对它做推理。
cues.en: We want to understand it, we want to reason about it.

cues.zh: 这就是科学。
cues.en: That's science.

cues.zh: 不过，自然世界真是个大麻烦。
cues.en: Now, the natural world is a real pain in the ass.

cues.zh: 我们可轻松多了。
cues.en: We've got it.

cues.zh: 所以，拜托，别抱怨自己是软件工程师。
cues.en: So, like, never complain about being a software engineer, please.

cues.zh: 因为我们这行实在太容易了。
cues.en: Because we have it so incredibly easy.

cues.zh: 呃，我们手上的东西又便宜又容易改。
cues.en: Um, we are, things are so cheap and malleable for us.

cues.zh: 相比之下，现实世界真是个大麻烦，你得做又大又昂贵的实验。
cues.en: Versus, in the real world, the real world is such a pain in the ass, where you have to do big, expensive experiments.

cues.zh: 而且你不能对要做什么毫无概念就去做实验。
cues.en: And you can't just like go into an experiment not having no idea of what you're trying to do.

cues.zh: 几乎从定义上，你就得以假设为中心。
cues.en: You've got to be almost by definition, very hypothesis-centric.

cues.zh: 你得先有个自己正在验证的猜想。
cues.en: You have to have a hunch that you're checking out.

cues.zh: 而且这个猜想，大概得是对的。
cues.en: And that hunch like probably needs to be right.

cues.zh: 然后你得设计实验来推翻这个猜想。
cues.en: Uh and then you need to design your experiment to invalidate that hunch.

cues.zh: 这很难，也很贵。
cues.en: It's it's hard, it's expensive.

cues.zh: 我们拥有一种难以置信的奢侈。
cues.en: We have got an incredible luxury.

cues.zh: 软件完全是人造的。
cues.en: Software is entirely synthetic.

cues.zh: 我们身处这些不可思议的、奢华的系统中，它们是一台人造的数学机器；而我们得出的结论往往不是“很可能为真”，而是“可证明为真”。
cues.en: We have, we live in this unbelievably uh this these luxurious systems of a synthetic mathematical machine and the conclusions that we draw are often not likely true, but provably true.

cues.zh: 这是一种极大的奢侈。
cues.en: Which is a tremendous luxury.

cues.zh: 而且我们做实验非常容易。
cues.en: And we can perform experiments so easily.

cues.zh: 做实验的成本太低了。
cues.en: They're so cheap to perform experiments.

cues.zh: 更重要的是，当我们对系统有疑问时，可以直接问它。
cues.en: And even more importantly, when we have questions of our systems, we can simply ask it.

cues.zh: 所有软件都是我们写的。
cues.en: We wrote all the software.

cues.zh: 这一切确实都是我们写的。
cues.en: We did actually write all this.

cues.zh: 我知道有时候感觉并非如此。
cues.en: I know sometimes it doesn't feel like that.

cues.zh: 这些其实都是我们写出来的。
cues.en: We actually wrote all this.

cues.zh: 我们是可以对它进行推理的。
cues.en: Like, we can reason about this.

cues.zh: 这不是一个已经演化了四十亿年的系统。
cues.en: This is not a system that has been evolving for 4 billion years.

cues.zh: 这是一个你看到的每一行代码都不到——怎么说呢——六十年历史的系统。
cues.en: This is a system that is every line of code you're looking at is less than what, 60 years old.

cues.zh: 而且其中大部分还要年轻得多，历史短得多。
cues.en: And and most of them are a lot less a lot younger than that.

cues.zh: 我们是可以理解它的。
cues.en: We can understand it.

cues.zh: 而且我们可以仅仅通过观察来理解软件。
cues.en: And we can understand software simply by observing it.

cues.zh: 我认为这是调试的一个关键认知。
cues.en: And I think that this is one of the key things to realize about debugging.

cues.zh: 调试的艺术——因为我觉得，当你身边有个很懂调试的人时，你可能看不懂他在做什么。
cues.en: The the art of debugging, because I think when you're around someone who understands how to debug very well, you might not understand what they're doing.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，他们多少是故意这样的。
cues.en: And by the way, they're kind of doing that intentionally.

cues.zh: 一个很会调试的人做事时会带点从容的意味，因为很容易出现这种情况：你知道，他们就这么消失一阵子。
cues.en: There's a little bit of leisure domain on the act of someone who can debug very well, in that it's very easy to, you know, they kind of disappear for a while.

cues.zh: 然后，瞧，修复方案就来了。
cues.en: Then, voila, I present the fix.

cues.zh: 就像在问，你是怎么想出来的？
cues.en: It's like, how did you figure that out?

cues.zh: 就像，哦，调试器从不多嘴。
cues.en: It's like, oh, a debugger never tells.

cues.zh: 哦，那是什么？
cues.en: Oh, what's that?

cues.zh: 你耳朵后面有枚硬币。
cues.en: You have a coin behind your ear.

cues.zh: 好，来了，Jimmy，你想要个气球吗？
cues.en: Okay, there we go, Jimmy, would you like a balloon?

cues.zh: 呃，我们其实想表达的是，我们就像魔术师。
cues.en: Um, so we we kind of like to kind of present this idea that we're like magicians.

cues.zh: 我们不是魔术师。
cues.en: We are not magicians.

cues.zh: 我们是《绿野仙踪》里的奥兹巫师，在帘子后面满头大汗、手忙脚乱地摇着曲柄，拼命想搞清楚问题。
cues.en: We are the Wizard of Oz sweating behind a curtain frenetically turning a crank trying to figure out the problem.

cues.zh: 调试厉害的人都懂这一点。
cues.en: And those that can debug well know this.

cues.zh: 调试差的人不知道这一点，因为他们调试得差，还缺乏自知之明。
cues.en: Those that debug poorly don't know this because they debug poorly and they suffer from self poor self awareness.

cues.zh: 调试就是提出问题并回答它们，而不是猜答案。
cues.en: Debugging is the act of asking questions and answering them, not guessing what the answer is.

cues.zh: 你是在玩
cues.en: You are playing

cues.zh: 二十问。
cues.en: 20 questions.

cues.en: And when I say 20 questions, I mean, not 20 questions with my children who are unbelievably annoying to play 20 questions with.

cues.zh: 于是他们就会说，好吧，来玩二十问。
cues.en: So they'll be like, okay, 20 questions play.

cues.zh: 好吧。
cues.en: All right.

cues.zh: 好吧，爸爸，它是獾吗？
cues.en: Okay, dad, is it a badger?

cues.zh: 我就说，不是，那……它是哺乳动物，还是动物，还是植物？
cues.en: I'm like, no, like, how about like, is it a mammal, or is it an animal, or is it a vegetable?

cues.zh: 他们就说，呃，但它是獾吗？
cues.en: It's like, uh, but is it a badger?

cues.zh: 我就说，不是，你听不懂吗？
cues.en: I'm like, no, don't you understand?

cues.zh: 他们又说，爸爸，它是獾吗？
cues.en: It's like, dad, is it a badger?

cues.zh: 你就会想，靠，它是獾吧，但该死，又不是。
cues.en: And you're like, fuck it is a badger, but damn it, it's like, they're not.

cues.zh: 嗯，就像我跟你……我承认，我改过二十问的答案，就为了教他们更重要的道理：要学会问更好的问题。
cues.en: Um, it's like I you and I have, I will confess, I have changed my answer to 20 questions just to like, teach teach them the larger lesson of like asking asking better questions.

cues.zh: 嗯，你要提出的是问题，不是假设。
cues.en: Um, you want to form questions, not hypotheses.

cues.zh: 因为太常见了，人们会这样：哦，我知道它是什么，我知道这个。
cues.en: Because too often, what people do is they, oh, I know what it is, I know this.

cues.zh: 它就在那儿。
cues.en: It's over there.

cues.zh: 哦，我修好了，已经合进去了，已经推送了。
cues.en: Oh, I fixed it, it's in, it's pushed.

cues.zh: 就像，等等，等等，等等，等等。
cues.en: It's like, whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa.

cues.zh: 等等，我们怎么会从你猜它是什么、把它修好、推上去，到“哦，我们没再见到它了”？
cues.en: Whoa, how did we go from you guessing what it was, having it fixed, pushing it, oh, we didn't see it again?

cues.zh: 嗯，我们没再见到它，这其实并不能证明你的假设是对的。
cues.en: Well, we didn't see it again, that's not actually that that doesn't actually prove your hypothesis correct.

cues.zh: 我们应该不断提问。
cues.en: We should be asking questions.

cues.zh: 当这些问题给出答案时，这些答案就是事实，而这些事实会约束假设。
cues.en: And as those questions give answers, those answers are facts, and those facts constrain hypotheses.

cues.zh: 然后我们重复这个过程：问题的答案引出更具体的问题，更具体的答案，更具体的问题，更具体的答案。
cues.en: And we repeat this process of answers to questions making more specific questions, more specific answers, more specific questions, more specific answers.

cues.zh: 于是，那个假设性的跳跃往往根本算不上跳跃。
cues.en: And then that hypothetical leap is often not a leap at all.

cues.zh: 那只是跨过一个小水坑的一步。
cues.en: It's a step across a puddle.

cues.zh: 我这辈子调试过很多棘手的 bug。
cues.en: And I've debugged a lot of nasty bugs in my life.

cues.en: That has always been the process.

cues.zh: 而且有很多很多很多很多很多很多 bug，即使我离最终原因——根因——只有几纳米，我仍然不敢相信。
cues.en: And there have been many, many, many, many, many, many bugs where the the even as I was nanometers away from the final cause, the root cause, I still couldn't believe it.

cues.zh: 只有当你真正得到最终答案时，你才会想：天哪，这是微处理器 bug 之类的问题。
cues.en: And it was only when you actually get to that final answer, you're like, oh my god, this is a microprocessor bug or what have you.

cues.zh: 嗯，这就是我们调试的方式。
cues.en: Um, so that is the way we debug.

cues.zh: 我们调试，就是通过一轮又一轮的提问和回答。
cues.en: We we we debug by having the the the cycle of of questions and answers.

cues.zh: 嗯，这有很多形式。
cues.en: Um, and this takes many forms.

cues.zh: 呃，这意味着，我们如何向软件提问？
cues.en: Uh, it means that, you know, how do we how do we ask questions of software?

cues.zh: 尤其是我们这些软件开发者，该如何设计软件？
cues.en: And in particular, those of us that are software developers, how do we design our software?

cues.zh: 让它能回答关于自身的问题。
cues.en: To answer questions about itself.

cues.zh: 如果说调试的艺术在于提问，那么编写可调试软件的技艺就在于设计软件。
cues.en: That if if the art of debugging is asking questions, the craft of writing debuggable software is designing your software.

cues.zh: 让别人能够向它提问。
cues.en: For someone else to be able to ask questions of it.

cues.zh: 这意味着要为事后调试而设计。
cues.en: It means designing for postmortem debuggability.

cues.zh: 当这个东西崩溃时，我会生成核心转储。
cues.en: When this thing dies, I generate a core dump.

cues.zh: 我是不是在地址空间周围留了面包屑，让人更容易弄清楚，或者更容易弄清发生了什么？
cues.en: Have I left the bread crumbs around my address space to make it easy to figure out, or easier to figure out what happened?

cues.zh: 这是为原位插桩而设计。
cues.en: It's designing for in situ instrumentation.

cues.zh: 是能在程序运行时对它进行插桩的能力。
cues.en: Be the ability to instrument something while it's running.

cues.zh: 嗯，还要考虑别人会想怎样给它插桩？
cues.en: Um, and it's thinking about like, how would someone want to instrument this?

cues.zh: 并利用 T trace 之类的东西。
cues.en: And leveraging things like T trace and so on.

cues.zh: 这是为事后调试而设计。
cues.en: It's designing for post-hoc debugging.

cues.zh: 事后调试，完全是在事情发生之后。
cues.en: Post-hoc debugging, totally after the fact.

cues.zh: 日志记录。
cues.en: Logging.

cues.zh: 日志记录非常非常有用，对吧？
cues.en: Logging is very, very helpful, right?

cues.zh: 显然，日志记录也有风险，嗯，但记录日志、知道该记什么、什么时候记，这就是编写可调试软件的手艺。
cues.en: And you obviously logging, there's a peril to logging as well, um, but logging and knowing what to log and when to log, that's the craft of of writing debuggable software.

cues.zh: 而且必须避免在生产环境中调试，因为你绝不想在故障期间调试。
cues.en: And it it's essential to avoid debugging in production, because you really don't want to debug during an outage.

cues.zh: 要做到这点，一部分就是建立调试文化。
cues.en: Part of doing that is creating a culture of debugging.

cues.zh: 同样，当我们把调试看作理解系统、改进系统，而不只是让问题消失的过程，我们就能把调试奉为核心理念。
cues.en: Again, when we view debugging as understanding the system, improving the system, not merely as the process by which problems are made to go away, we can enshrine debugging.

cues.zh: 我们可以把它视为一等操作，并鼓励自己真正去追根溯源。
cues.en: We can think of this as a first-class operation, and we can encourage ourselves to actually root cause things.

cues.zh: 如果工程师闻到了烟味，就应该去查清根源。
cues.en: If an engineer smells smoke, they should root cause that.

cues.zh: 那是厨房着火了吗？
cues.en: If that's, is that a fire in the kitchen?

cues.zh: 是咖啡机吗？
cues.en: Is that the coffee maker?

cues.zh: 还是煤层里正在熊熊燃烧的大火？
cues.en: Or is that the fire raging in a coal seam?

cues.zh: 这种情况我在职业生涯里发现过太多次了。
cues.en: Which I've discovered way too many times in my career.

cues.zh: 这怎么可能跑得起来？
cues.en: How could this ever work?

cues.zh: 你有没有这样问过自己？
cues.en: You ever say that to yourself?

cues.zh: 我的天，这到底是怎么跑起来的？
cues.en: Oh my god, how did this how does anything work?

cues.zh: 结果发现全靠巧合。
cues.en: Turns out it's all by accident.

cues.zh: 就像，我的天，这到底是怎么跑起来的？
cues.en: It's like, oh my god, how does this ever work?

cues.zh: 你能找到问题所在，是因为出现了一个异常、一种现象，而你能把它完全恢复过来。
cues.en: The reason you got there is because there was an anomaly, a phenomenon out here that you were able to completely recover.

cues.zh: 但我们必须有一种鼓励这种做法的组织文化。
cues.en: But we must have an organizational culture that encourages that.

cues.zh: 绝不能让人觉得，哦，那是你的20%项目。那简直让我想揍你一顿。
cues.en: That must not be perceived as like, oh, that's your 20% project. It's like, I want to punch you in the face.

cues.zh: 呃，这不像是空闲时间的活动。
cues.en: Uh, it like that is not like a free time activity.

cues.zh: 这是我们交付的软件的核心部分。
cues.en: That is a core part of the software we are delivering.

cues.zh: 我们必须多花时间，把可调试性构建进去。
cues.en: And we've got to take the extra time to build for debuggability.

cues.zh: 这属于一个非常激进、有争议的理念，我称之为：第一次就做对。
cues.en: This is part of a very radical, controversial idea, I'm calling, do it right the first time.

cues.zh: 我知道。
cues.en: I know.

cues.zh: 我知道。
cues.en: I know.

cues.zh: 所以，第一次就做对。
cues.en: So do it right the first time.

cues.zh: 哦，从不。
cues.en: Oh, never.

cues.zh: 不，我们甚至第十五次都做不对。
cues.en: No, we don't even do it right the 15th time.

cues.zh: 就像，试着第一次就做对。
cues.en: It's like, try doing it right the first time.

cues.zh: 重写代价非常非常高。
cues.en: Rewrites are very, very expensive.

cues.zh: 而重写的代价，从来不会由引发它的那笔技术债来承担。
cues.en: And the cost of the rewrite is never borne by the technical debt that induced it.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，说白了，这些人往往已经跳槽去别的工作了。
cues.en: By the way, those people are often off to other jobs, just to put it bluntly.

cues.zh: 如果你想知道为什么，我一看简历，看到 18 个月、18 个月、18 个月、18 个月、18 个月，我就想要相当有说服力的答案。
cues.en: And if you're wondering why when I look at a resume, and I see 18 months, 18 months, 18 months, 18 months, 18 months, I want some pretty good answers.

cues.zh: 确实可能有好的答案。
cues.en: There can be good answers.

cues.zh: 也可能有很多好的答案。
cues.en: There can be lots of good answers.

cues.zh: 我创业失败、创业失败、创业还行、还行，好吧。
cues.en: I'm startup failed, startup failed, startup okay, okay, well.

cues.zh: 但还会发生的是，人们其实做了一堆糟糕的决定，然后跳到下一份工作。
cues.en: But what what also happens is that people actually make a bunch of bad decisions and move on to the next job.

cues.zh: 而那些为这些决定承担代价的人，只能在他们身后无声地呐喊。
cues.en: And those that bear the cost of those decisions are left silently screaming in their wake.

cues.zh: 所以我们必须有一种文化，鼓励我们第一次就把事情做对。
cues.en: So we have to have a culture that encourages us to do things correctly the first time.

cues.zh: 那么，发生故障时我们该怎么做？
cues.en: So, how do we do during an outage?

cues.zh: 嗯，故障期间，每个人都会看清自己到底是谁。
cues.en: Well, during an outage, everyone is going to discover whether they are who they actually are.

cues.zh: 说到 DevOps、hug ops，说要拉近关系——这很棒。我完全支持 hug ops。
cues.en: When we say Devops, hug ops, like let's get that's great. I'm all about like hug ops.

cues.zh: 但归根结底，抱歉，你要么是开发者，要么是运维人员。
cues.en: But at the end of the day, I'm sorry, you are a developer, or you are an operator.

cues.zh: 我们可以非常紧密，可以彼此高度共情，也应该如此。
cues.en: We can get very close together, we can have very tight empathy for one another, and we should.

cues.zh: 但这一刻，你会认清自己是什么。
cues.en: But this is the moment that you'll know what you are.

cues.zh: 当你遇到一个服务：它还在运行，但已经受损。
cues.en: The moment you've got a service, the service is up but impaired.

cues.zh: 你知道重启服务能恢复对客户的服务，但会丢失信息，让你无法调试。
cues.en: You know that restarting the service will restore service to your customers, but it will lose information such that you cannot debug it.

cues.zh: 如果是运维人员，就会说：看，必须重启它。
cues.en: If an inner operator will be like, look, got to restart it.

cues.zh: 内心的开发者会说：看，得调试它。
cues.en: An inner developer would be like, look, got to debug it.

cues.zh: 就像，得重启它。
cues.en: It's like, got to restart it.

cues.zh: 真的得调试它。
cues.en: Really need to debug it.

cues.zh: 所以，别陷入虚假的二分法，重启和调试都得做。
cues.en: Okay, so you need to not get trapped into a false dichotomy, you need to both restart it and debug it.

cues.zh: 呃，还要找到具体办法。
cues.en: Uh, and find the ways.

cues.zh: 如何在不丢失信息的情况下恢复服务？
cues.en: How do we resume service without losing information?

cues.zh: 在信息损失最小的前提下，我们能恢复到什么程度的服务？
cues.en: What degree of service can we resume with minimal loss of information?

cues.zh: 我们不想过度强调恢复，而忽略理解系统如何运作。
cues.en: We do not want to overemphasize recovery with respect to understanding the way the system works.

cues.zh: 我们不想如此迷信恢复，以至于不再理解系统，还相信只要一直重启所有东西，坏掉的软件就能弥补问题。
cues.en: We don't want to so believe in recovery, that we that that we actually no longer understand the system, and that we believe that broken software can simply be made up for things by restarting everything all of the time.

cues.zh: 这就像，那叫 Windows，人类做过这个实验，但没成功。
cues.en: It's like, that's called Windows, and humanity did that experiment and it didn't work.

cues.zh: 可以吗？
cues.en: Okay?

cues.zh: 所以我们其实需要理解这些系统是如何工作的。
cues.en: So we actually need to understand the way these systems work.

cues.zh: 我们确实需要；如果我们用恢复机制取代对故障软件的实际理解，就是在让坏掉的软件变成常态。
cues.en: We do if we we if we enshrine recovery in lieu of actually understanding broken software, we normalize broken software.

cues.zh: 软件不该是坏的。
cues.en: Software should not be broken.

cues.zh: 在我们所制造的东西中，软件尤其不该是坏的。
cues.en: Uniquely among the things we make, software should not be broken.

cues.zh: 老天，它可是台数学机器。
cues.en: It's a mathematical machine, for Christ's sake.

cues.zh: 它不会磨损。把它做对。
cues.en: It does not wear out. Get it right.

cues.zh: 拜托。
cues.en: Please.

cues.zh: 我们恰恰能把它做对。
cues.en: We uniquely can get it right.

cues.zh: 如果你把“软件总是坏的”这个观念根植于心，就会带来各种糟糕后果。
cues.en: And if you engrain this idea that software is always broken, there are all sorts of bad things that come from this.

cues.zh: 比如“软件应该容忍坏输入”这种想法。
cues.en: The idea that software should tolerate bad input.

cues.zh: 不，它不该。
cues.en: No, it shouldn't.

cues.zh: 软件应该显式地失败。
cues.en: Software should fail fail explicitly.

cues.zh: 如果你想恶搞，肯定能让某个资深工程师一整天都干不了活，你就说：嘿，你知道我可以运行 npm install 而不是 install，而且它居然真能用吗？
cues.en: If you want to troll, certainly any giant engineer and not being productive for the rest of the day, say, hey, did you know that I can do npm install instead of install, and it will actually work?

cues.zh: 她会说：“这时候机器人正乐呵呵地提供东西，然后……”
cues.en: And she'd be like, This is when like the bot is cheerfully offering things and get.

cues.zh: 嗯，软件应该能从致命故障中恢复。
cues.en: Um, software should recover from fatal failures.

cues.zh: 不，不应该。
cues.en: No, it shouldn't.

cues.zh: 如果你有未捕获的异常，你对人类的责任就是去死。
cues.en: If you have an uncaught exception, it is your duty to humanity to die.

cues.zh: 生成你的全部状态，把你那具防腐过的尸体呈给 Quincy Emmy。
cues.en: Generate all of your state, present your embalmed carcass to those to Quincy Emmy.

cues.zh: 抱歉，我没法拿 Quincy Emmy 玩梗。
cues.en: I cannot make a Quincy Emmy reference, I'm sorry.

cues.zh: 你不知道 Quincy Emmy 是什么，不怪你。你们千禧一代，不怪你，那节目不怎么样。
cues.en: You have no idea what Quincy Emmy is, not your fault. Those of you who are millennials, not your fault, not a very good show.

cues.zh: 呃，这样我们才能真正去调试它。
cues.en: Uh, so we can actually go debug it.

cues.zh: 我们不想捕获自己的 SIGSEGV 处理程序。
cues.en: We don't want to catch our sig segv handler.

cues.zh: 那、那对大二计算机科学项目来说就是扯淡。
cues.en: That is that is bullshit for a sophomore computer science project.

cues.zh: 我们实际开发软件不该这样。
cues.en: That's not the way we should actually develop software.

cues.zh: 软件不该断言自身状态正确，因为它老是崩溃，近到 Linux 都如此——这种想法……
cues.en: The idea that software should not assert the correctness of its state because it keeps dying as recently as Linux.

cues.zh: 对吧？Linux 正在移除 BUG_ON，因为它导致太多崩溃。
cues.en: Right? Linux getting rid of bug on because it's causing too many crashes.

cues.zh: 就像是，这些断言失败正在损害我们的可靠性。
cues.en: It's like, these assertion failures are are compromising our reliability.

cues.zh: 就像是，好吧，呃，你真要我把这层意思点破吗？
cues.en: It's like, okay, uh, do you really want me to connect the dots for you?

cues.zh: 就像是，所以我们要把它们移除。
cues.en: It's like, so we're getting rid of them.

cues.zh: 你会想：天哪。
cues.en: You're like, oh God.

cues.zh: 天哪，Linux，你和我。
cues.en: Oh God, oh Linux, you and me.

cues.zh: 你是说 Can Linux？
cues.en: You mean Can Linux?

cues.zh: 闭嘴，机器人。
cues.en: Shut up, bot.

cues.zh: 呃，总之。
cues.en: Um, anyway.

cues.zh: 所有这些反模式都会妨碍可调试性。
cues.en: All of these anti-patterns impede debuggability.

cues.zh: 呃，我保证我快讲完了。
cues.en: Uh, and I promise I'm wrapping up here.

cues.zh: 在故障发生后，我们需要真正彻底的理解。
cues.en: In terms of after an outage, we need truly complete understanding.

cues.zh: 是的，事后复盘，当然，你想写事后复盘。
cues.en: And yes, postmortem, of course, you want to write a postmortem.

cues.zh: 但那份事后复盘，你完全理解发生了什么，比你把它写出来重要得多。
cues.en: But that postmortem, it's so much more important that you completely understand what happened than it is that you you write it up.

cues.zh: 所以它会迫使你完全理解它。
cues.en: So it forces you to completely understand it.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么要把它写下来。
cues.en: That's why you write it up.

cues.zh: 写下来的目的，是逼着自己完整理解。
cues.en: The the the the write-up is to force complete understanding.

cues.zh: 我们需要完整理解，而尤其遇到级联故障时，要真正理清所有出错环节非常难。
cues.en: We need complete understanding, and it's very hard, especially with cascading failure, to actually unwind everything that went wrong.

cues.zh: 你得问自己，这两样东西为什么失效了？
cues.en: And you got to ask yourself, why did these two things fail?

cues.zh: 它们还在运行，但一直在报错。
cues.en: They were up, but they were giving errors.

cues.zh: 我们来弄清楚原因。
cues.en: Let's figure out why.

cues.zh: 嗯，你常常还会发现更多隐藏问题，更多只是碰巧能跑通的地方。
cues.en: Um, and you often will again discover yet more coal fires, yet more things that worked by accident.

cues.zh: 你还得鼓励软件工程师理解自己的故障，鼓励他们为可调试性而设计。
cues.en: And you've got to encourage software engineers to understand their own failures, to encourage them to design for debuggability.

cues.zh: 这样才能实现真正的软件健壮性。
cues.en: That gets us to true software robustness.

cues.zh: 我们需要区分运行故障——系统整体上出了问题——和程序性故障。
cues.en: We need to differentiate operational failure, something that went wrong in the system at at large, versus programmatic failure.

cues.zh: 程序性故障，就得真的让它挂掉。
cues.en: Programmatic failure, you need to actually die.

cues.zh: 运行性故障，必须真正去处理。
cues.en: Operational failure needs to actually be handled.

cues.zh: 所以，你看，这总会很有压力。
cues.en: So, look, it's always going to be stressful.

cues.zh: 服务宕机时，你总会恨不得吐在键盘上。
cues.en: You're always going to want to throw up on your keyboard when a service is down.

cues.zh: 这不会——我不是想把这事说得很轻松。
cues.en: This is not going to be I'm not going to hear to make this easy.

cues.zh: 这并不容易。
cues.en: It's not easy.

cues.zh: 嗯，服务宕机时，我们得做一些艰难的选择。
cues.en: Um and when a service is down, we've got some tough choices to make.

cues.zh: 嗯，我我觉得，要按长时间故障来准备。
cues.en: Um I I think plan for a long outage.

cues.zh: 嗯，要计划，呃，计划尽可能多地收集信息来调试。
cues.en: Um plan to uh plan to gather as much information as you can to debug it.

cues.zh: 每一步都要小心。
cues.en: Be careful when you step.

cues.zh: 失误的代价真的非常非常高。
cues.en: Missteps are really, really costly.

cues.zh: 我在故障中常看到的问题是，早期的一次失误会让情况雪上加霜。
cues.en: Often a failure that I see in outages is that they are exacerbated by an early misstep.

cues.zh: 看看 GitLab 那次故障，GitLab 故障中删错了数据库。
cues.en: Look at the GitLab outage, the wrong database was deleted in the GitLab outage.

cues.zh: 为什么删错了数据库？
cues.en: Why was the wrong database deleted?

cues.zh: 因为他们当时还有另一个问题。
cues.en: Because they were having another problem.

cues.zh: 他们已经陷在另一个问题里，相对而言那是个更小的问题，然后那位著名的操作员删错了数据库。
cues.en: They were already in another problem that was relatively speaking a more minor problem, and the the the famous operator one deleted the wrong database.

cues.zh: 那是他们采取的一个动作，之所以这么做，是因为他们想把系统恢复上线。
cues.en: That was an act that was they they're doing that because they they want to get the system back up.

cues.zh: 对，你想把系统恢复上线。
cues.en: Yes, you want to get the system back up.

cues.zh: 但请停下来想一想。
cues.en: But please, stop and think.

cues.zh: 拜托。
cues.en: Please.

cues.zh: 这值得做——好吧，大家离开键盘，我们开个电话会议，好吗？
cues.en: It's worthwhile to, okay, everybody, away from the keyboard, can we have a concall please?

cues.zh: 我们开个电话会议，把一些想法说出来吧。
cues.en: Let's have a concall and can we just let's get some ideas out there.

cues.zh: 我们可以去问哪些问题？
cues.en: What are some questions that we can go ask?

cues.zh: 如果 Three Mile Island 事故时他们也这么做——大家都离开控制台一会儿。
cues.en: If in Three Mile Island, they had done that, everybody away from the console for a second.

cues.zh: 让我们花点时间，认真想一想。
cues.en: Let's take a second and really think.

cues.zh: 他们其实会发现，飞行员当时真的以为那个东西是开着的。
cues.en: They would have actually figured out that the pilot operator really thought was open.

cues.zh: 事实上，正是交接班的人发现了问题。
cues.en: Indeed it was the shift change that figured it out.

cues.zh: 因为新来的人一进来就说，等等，原来是这么回事。
cues.en: Because fresh minds came in like, wait a minute, this is what's going on.

cues.zh: 让不同团队从不同方向调查，并行推进。
cues.en: Paralyze by having different teams take different avenues of investigation.

cues.zh: 把这些故障视为机会。
cues.en: And view these outages as an opportunity.

cues.zh: 它们让我们理解自己的软件，更重要的是，围绕软件培养一种重视可调试性的文化。
cues.en: They allow us to understand our software and, more importantly, develop a a culture around software that values debuggability.
